CNN, the Wall Street Journal, Axios, and others all relied on identical wire-style phrasing — "steps down as chairman" — with no loaded adjectives or ideological framing. The Financial Times took a successor-focused angle, using the neutral verb "succeed" to foreground Howard Buffett's appointment. CNBC appended Buffett's own quote, "Father Time always wins," adding color without editorial spin. The only mild departure was MarketWatch, which used the word "reign" and pivoted toward investment advice — "fans should sell Berkshire" — introducing a slightly more opinionated, commercially oriented frame. Even so, this reflects a financial-analysis angle rather than ideological bias. Overall, the story was treated as straightforward business news with no meaningful political or partisan framing detectable across any outlet.

The core framing fault line, then, is whether AI safety concerns represent legitimate policy imperatives or unfounded panic.
